name: No profile can execute shell commands — cards needing git/pytest are unrunnable (blocks 4 committed cards)
description:
## The finding

Four of the eight open `IT team` cards cannot be executed by *any* profile, because the task toolset **has no command / shell tool**. Evidence collected on 2026-11-18:

1. **Card `9ce4e7ef` run (10:20 UTC, profile `repository`, 3 messages, `progress: 0`):** the agent's own verdict — *"I have no shell/command tool in this task's toolset"* — after which it produced a read-only manifest instead of the archive. The card is **not** done; no backup exists.
2. **Corroborated from the manager side:** the ProjectManager toolset in the same session contains `project_map/locate/trace/impact/health`, `project_read_file/write_file/changes`, `read_folder`, `search_codx`, `project_manager`, `create_task`, `process_task`, `list_profiles*`, `profile_knowledge_search`, `fetch_webpage`, `web_search`, `doc_converter` — **and no command execution**. So the manager cannot run `git` either.
3. **Counter-evidence that must be reconciled:** on 2026-11-17 the QA card `d7e0f3fa` produced a real `pytest` run and an untracked `pytest-qa-report.xml`. So either one profile (`qa` / `qa_automation`) *does* hold an execution tool, or that run happened outside a card. **Do not assume fleet-wide absence — establish it per profile.**

## Impact on committed dates

Every one of these needs to execute a command, and none of them can be closed by an agent today:
- `88d57bdd` — needs `git add`/`git commit` for 4 clusters (high, due 19 Nov)
- `9ce4e7ef` — needs `tar`/`git diff` for the backup (high, due today)
- `d7e0f3fa` — needs the test edited and `pytest` re-run (high, due 19 Nov)
- `e5841226` — needs the collected-test count from a real run (due 20 Nov)

This is the *second* structural cause of the three consecutive "blocked" shift reports, after the atlas timeouts (`d8534b12`). It is more dangerous than the atlas bug, because it looks like an agent failure while it is a configuration gap.

## Do this

1. Enumerate, for each profile used by this board (`repository`, `software_developer`, `qa`, `qa_automation`, `ciso`, `ProjectManager`), the granted tools — from the profile definition / grants, not by trying a task and watching it fail.
2. Identify the exact tool that made the 17 Nov `pytest` run possible. If it exists, name it.
3. Grant an execution tool to the profiles that must run repository commands (`repository`, `software_developer`, `qa_automation`), scoped so a card cannot run destructive git commands — the constraint "never `git checkout/restore/stash/reset/clean` on this tree" must be enforced, not merely written in a description.
4. Document the result in the profile docs so the next manager stop assigning shell work to read-only profiles.

## Acceptance

- A card processed with the `repository` profile runs `git status --porcelain=v1 | wc -l` and pastes the real number (currently **59** files changed outside `.codx/` churn).
- A written matrix profile → execution tool (yes/no) is on this card.
- `9ce4e7ef` can then be completed by an agent without a human terminal.

Do **not** use the atlas tools on this repo while `d8534b12` is open — they hang for 120 s and will eat the run.

messages.content: Establish, per profile, which ones can execute shell commands. Card `9ce4e7ef` failed with "I have no shell/command tool in this task's toolset"; the manager toolset has none either; yet QA produced a real pytest run on 17 Nov, so the capability exists somewhere. Enumerate the grants, name the execution tool, and grant it to the profiles that need it.

**Evidence added by ProjectManager, 2026-11-18 10:24 UTC — first row of the matrix is now measured, not assumed.**

I enumerated the granted tools of the `repository` profile (the profile I assigned to the backup card `9ce4e7ef`, because it is the closest fit for git work). Its full `tools` list is:

```
repository_overview · repository_status · repository_branches · repository_log
repository_compare · repository_commit_message · get_file_last_version
project_read_file · project_search · project_grep · project_glob · search_codx
```

**Twelve tools, zero execution.** It can *read* git state (`repository_status`, `repository_log`, `repository_compare`) and *write a commit message*, but it cannot run `git add`, `git commit`, `tar`, `pytest` or any shell command. That is why `9ce4e7ef` returned progress 0 with "I have no shell/command tool in this task's toolset" — the profile is correct for the work, the toolset is missing the capability.

Also checked: `search_codx("shell", modules=["profiles"])` returns **no matches** in any profile definition, so this is not one misconfigured profile.

## What this means for the acceptance criteria

- "A card processed with `repository` runs `git status --porcelain=v1` and pastes the number" — **`repository_status` may already satisfy this without a shell**; verify whether it returns porcelain-equivalent output before concluding the whole matrix is red.
- "A written matrix profile → execution tool (yes/no)" — start from this measured row and add: `software_developer`, `qa_automation`, `ciso`, `codx-junior`, `file_editor`. A profile that can *write files* does not automatically run commands; distinguish write-capable (`project_write_file`) from execute-capable.
- The four blocked cards (`9ce4e7ef`, `88d57bdd`, `d7e0f3fa`, `e5841226`) all need *execute*. If no profile has it, the fix is either an execution tool granted to a profile, or a documented human step. Decide which, and say so on this card — that is the deliverable.

## Correction of my own ruling — do not action this card as written (ProjectManager, shift 3)

**My earlier ruling on this card was wrong, and I am withdrawing it.** I wrote that this was "a profile-grant configuration change, executable with file tools, no shell needed", demoable at 13:30 today. That is not true. Evidence gathered this shift:

1. `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` — 1968 lines, the tool registry. Pattern search for `command|execute|terminal|subprocess|bash` returns 4 hits, **all the same tool**: `security_check_command` (import L245, name L427, registry entry ~L1855). It validates a command string and **executes nothing**.
2. `search_codx(modules=["profiles"], query="shell")` → **no matches** across all 9 profile files.

**There is no shell tool, so no profile can be granted one.** A grant change cannot create a capability. This is a missing-tool engineering task.

## Disposition — this card is repurposed, not closed
- **`e816cc41-81a9-40fe-a686-2376722e2b4d`** (child of this card, `high`, due 18 Nov, **wake today 13:30**) now carries the build: author `run_command`, register it, wire `security_check_command` as pre-flight guard, with acceptance evidence.
- **This card (`18bca0e1`) becomes the enablement step**: after `e816cc41` lands, grant `run_command` per profile — `software_developer` and the repository profile first, **never globally**. Wake moved to **19 Nov 10:00** so nothing burns budget here before the tool exists.

## Note for the fleet — do not retry the premise
Do not re-investigate "which profile has shell". Answered. Start from `e816cc41`.

## Closed as rejected — superseded, not wrong

This card's premise ("grant an execution tool to the profiles that must run repository commands" / "enumerate the granted tools per profile") was disproven in source, so it cannot be executed as written:

- A profile **allowlist is not the gate**: `Profile.tools` defaults to `[]` (`codx/junior/model/profile.py:142`) and **no** `.codx` profile JSON has a `tools` key (`search_codx(modules=["profiles"], query='"tools"')` → no matches). There was nothing to grant.
- The capability itself did not exist: the only command-related entry in `TOOLS` is `security_check_command`, which validates a string and executes nothing.
- Testing exists as a tool after all: `qa_run_tests` (plus `qa_plan`, `qa_review_changes`, `qa_coverage`, `qa_flaky_check`, `qa_policy`) — which is the likely explanation for the 17 Nov `pytest` run this card treated as counter-evidence. Do not re-open that question.
- The real, narrow need is now `e816cc41-81a9-40fe-a686-2376722e2b4d`: `repository_stage` + `repository_commit` were implemented and registered (no general shell, by explicit scope correction), pending process reload and a one-line fix tracked in `76d97f04-a902-43fa-980b-c873d719ef5b`.

Status `rejected`, progress 100, `wake_at` cleared so it does not fire again. Successor: `e816cc41`. Related environment finding (agent-side absence of shell/tar for card `9ce4e7ef`): `9ce4e7ef` keeps its own wake and is *not* closed by this — archiving the tree still needs `tar`, which the new two tools deliberately do not provide.
